learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes, and a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: first membrane event
items.prompt: A plasma-membrane protein binds an extracellular neurotransmitter. Within milliseconds, its pore opens and sodium ions enter the cell. Which class best matches the first controlled step?
options: A receptor enzyme that phosphorylates a cytosolic target
A ligand-gated ion channel that opens an ion-conducting pore
A G protein–coupled receptor that first activates a G protein
Not sure yet
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: identify the trigger
items.prompt: Depolarization changes the conformation of a membrane protein, after which calcium ions enter the cell. Which trigger–mechanism pairing is supported?
options: Ligand binding opens a ligand-gated calcium channel
GTP binding opens a pore inside a G protein–coupled receptor
Ligand binding activates a receptor enzyme that transports calcium
A voltage change opens a voltage-gated calcium channel
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: classify the receptor
items.prompt: A ligand causes two membrane receptors to associate, and their cytosolic domains phosphorylate themselves. No ions cross through the receptors. Which class is most consistent with these observations?
options: Receptor enzyme
Voltage-gated ion channel
Ligand-gated ion channel
G protein–coupled receptor
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: order the GPCR step
items.prompt: A ligand binds a seven-transmembrane receptor. Which event is expected earliest on the intracellular side in the G protein–coupled mechanism?
options: The ligand enters the nucleus and binds DNA
The receptor opens a pore that conducts sodium ions
G alpha releases GDP and binds GTP
The receptor directly phosphorylates every downstream target
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: voltage sensor
items.prompt: A mutation locks the voltage-sensing region of a voltage-gated sodium channel in its resting conformation. The membrane still depolarizes. What is the most immediate consequence?
options: The receptor enzyme stops phosphorylating its substrate
The channel stays closed, reducing sodium entry
G alpha fails to exchange GDP for GTP
The steroid receptor fails to enter the nucleus
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: blocked nucleotide exchange
items.prompt: A G protein–coupled receptor binds its ligand and changes conformation normally, but G alpha cannot release GDP. What is the earliest downstream consequence?
options: The ligand must diffuse through the plasma membrane
The receptor converts into a ligand-gated channel
The receptor directly phosphorylates nuclear DNA
G alpha stays inactive and cannot regulate its effector
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: direct membrane mechanism
items.prompt: Which observation most specifically supports a gated-channel mechanism rather than a receptor enzyme or G protein–coupled receptor?
options: A transcriptional response appears hours after stimulation
A second messenger rises after an effector enzyme is activated
An ion current begins when the membrane protein gate opens
A cytosolic receptor domain phosphorylates a target protein
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: ligand-gated chloride channel
items.prompt: An extracellular ligand still binds its chloride channel, but a pore mutation prevents chloride passage. What immediate response is lost?
options: The ligand-triggered chloride current
The G-alpha nucleotide-exchange response
The receptor-enzyme phosphorylation response
The nuclear steroid-receptor response
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: GPCR sequence
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders the first steps of G protein–coupled receptor signaling?
options: Effector activation → ligand binding → GDP release → receptor change
Ligand binding → receptor change → GDP/GTP exchange → effector regulation
Pore opening → ion flow → receptor phosphorylation → DNA binding
Ligand diffusion → nuclear binding → GTP hydrolysis → pore opening
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: effector coupling
items.prompt: A receptor activates G alpha and G alpha binds GTP, but the activated subunit cannot contact its effector enzyme. Which result is most immediate?
options: Extracellular ligand binding to the receptor
GDP-for-GTP exchange on activated G alpha
Effector regulation by activated G alpha
Voltage-gated ion conduction through the receptor
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: fused-ring signal
items.prompt: An endocrine signal has four fused carbon rings and few polar groups. Which early signaling behavior is most plausible from these facts?
options: It remains only in extracellular water because the rings are ionic
It forms an ion channel by itself in the plasma membrane
It can cross the bilayer and bind an intracellular receptor
Not sure yet
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: steroid sequence
items.prompt: A cortisol-like steroid crosses the plasma membrane. Which sequence best matches an intracellular-receptor mechanism?
options: Bind intracellular receptor → receptor complex regulates transcription
Open ligand-gated pore → sodium influx → membrane depolarization
Bind receptor enzyme → receptor transports the steroid through a pore
Bind G protein directly → exchange GDP for GTP on the hormone
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: isoprene cue
items.prompt: Which structural clue most directly supports classification in the terpene or terpenoid family?
options: A backbone built from repeating amino-acid units
A backbone built from repeating sugar-phosphate units
A core built from four fused carbon rings
A skeleton built from repeating five-carbon isoprene units
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: modified terpene
items.prompt: A signaling molecule retains an isoprene-derived carbon skeleton but contains added oxygen-bearing functional groups. Which classification is most appropriate?
options: Steroid protein
Terpenoid
Ligand-gated channel
Phospholipid bilayer
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: nuclear receptor block
items.prompt: A hydrophobic four-ring hormone enters a target cell, but its nuclear receptor is blocked. Which response should be reduced most directly?
options: Hormone-dependent regulation of transcription
Opening of a voltage-gated sodium channel by depolarization
Diffusion of oxygen through the membrane
Ligand-triggered ion flow through a membrane pore
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: oxygenated isoprenoid signal
items.prompt: A lipophilic, oxygenated, isoprene-derived signal still changes transcription in cells that lack the relevant membrane receptor enzyme but retain a nuclear receptor. Which relation is best supported?
options: An oxygenated signal must use a membrane pore
A transcription-changing signal must be a peptide
A terpenoid-like signal can use an intracellular receptor
A nuclear receptor must be a voltage-gated channel
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: receptor-step consequence
items.prompt: A steroid hormone enters a target cell and binds its intracellular receptor, but the receptor cannot bind target DNA. Which response should decrease most directly?
options: Depolarization-dependent opening of a voltage-gated calcium channel
Vesicular release of an unrelated peptide hormone
Ligand-triggered autophosphorylation by a membrane receptor enzyme
Hormone-dependent regulation of transcription by the receptor complex
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: nuclear entry block
items.prompt: A lipophilic four-ring hormone enters a target cell and binds its cytosolic receptor, but the hormone–receptor complex cannot move into the nucleus. Which response should be reduced most directly?
options: Ligand-triggered ion flow through a membrane pore
Receptor-dependent regulation of nuclear transcription
Depolarization-triggered sodium entry through a voltage-gated channel
Autophosphorylation by a membrane receptor enzyme
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: distinguish lipid-derived families
items.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two structural families used in this lesson?
options: Steroids and terpenes are classified by receptor location
Terpenes have fused rings, while steroids have peptide repeats
Steroids have fused rings, while terpenes have isoprene units
Terpenoids form ion channels, while steroids form receptor enzymes
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify and locate
items.prompt: A new messenger is an oxygenated derivative of an isoprene-built scaffold. Experiments show that it crosses the membrane and binds a nuclear receptor. Which description is best?
options: A terpenoid with an intracellular signaling role
A steroid defined solely by its nuclear receptor
A ligand-gated channel with a terpenoid pore
A peptide hormone with an isoprene backbone
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Prerequisite check: control-loop order
items.prompt: A sensory neuron detects a change, the central nervous system integrates the information, and an autonomic output changes an organ’s activity. Which order preserves the prior sensor–integration–effector model?
options: Effector → sensor → integration
Integration → effector → sensor
Effector → integration → sensor
Sensor → integration → effector
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: target is not source
items.prompt: A pituitary hormone stimulates the thyroid gland. Which source–product pair is correct?
options: Thyroid gland produces TSH
Anterior pituitary produces TSH
Posterior pituitary synthesizes thyroid hormone
Hypothalamus releases TSH into the systemic circulation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: synthesis and release
items.prompt: Which mapping correctly describes vasopressin (ADH) associated with the posterior pituitary?
options: Synthesized and released by the thyroid gland
Synthesized by the posterior pituitary and released by the hypothalamus
Synthesized in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary
Synthesized by the adrenal cortex and released from the adrenal medulla
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: adrenal region
items.prompt: Which source and chemical type correctly map to cortisol?
options: Adrenal cortex; steroid hormone
Adrenal medulla; peptide hormone
Posterior pituitary; catecholamine
Pancreatic beta cell; thyroid hormone
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: neck gland map
items.prompt: A gland in the anterior neck produces the major thyroid hormones T3 and T4. Which gland is described?
options: Anterior pituitary
Parathyroid gland
Adrenal cortex
Thyroid gland
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: neuroendocrine lesion
items.prompt: Axons connecting hypothalamic neurons to the posterior pituitary are severed, while the anterior pituitary remains intact. Release of which hormones is most directly reduced?
options: TSH and ACTH
ADH and oxytocin
Insulin and glucagon
Cortisol and aldosterone
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: location–product pair
items.prompt: Which location–product pair is correctly matched?
options: Adrenal medulla — epinephrine
Anterior pituitary — insulin
Pancreatic beta cell — cortisol
Thyroid gland — ACTH
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: pancreatic source
items.prompt: After blood glucose rises, a pancreatic islet cell releases a hormone that promotes glucose uptake and storage. Which source–product pair fits?
options: Alpha cell — glucagon
Adrenal cortex — insulin
Beta cell — insulin
Posterior pituitary — glucagon
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: synthesis versus release
items.prompt: Which statement correctly resolves the hypothalamus–posterior-pituitary relation?
options: The posterior pituitary synthesizes hypothalamic releasing hormones
The hypothalamus releases TSH directly from the thyroid
The anterior pituitary stores hormones synthesized by the hypothalamus
The hypothalamus makes ADH and oxytocin for posterior-pituitary release
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: reduced synthesis
items.prompt: The posterior pituitary is structurally intact, but hypothalamic synthesis of oxytocin is strongly inhibited. Which outcome is most likely after existing stores are depleted?
options: The posterior pituitary begins independent oxytocin synthesis
Oxytocin release falls after posterior-pituitary stores are depleted
The anterior pituitary becomes the new source of oxytocin
The adrenal medulla converts epinephrine into oxytocin
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
